responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the RISC-V architecture, covering target option parsing, ISA-extension modeling, ABI and OS/subtarget configuration, instruction selection, scheduling, builtins, vector support, and late target-specific optimization. Its core files (`riscv.cc`/`riscv.h`/`riscv.md` and `riscv.opt`) define the main target hooks, calling convention, frame and address handling, command-line `-m` options, and the central RTL machine description for scalar code generation, while companion `.md` families add support for atomics and memory models, PIC, compressed and bit-manipulation instructions, crypto, conditional operations, and vendor extensions such as T-Head, SiFive, CORE-V, MIPS, and Ventana. A major subarea is RVV support: `vector*.md`, `autovec*.md`, `riscv-v*.cc`, the `riscv-vector-builtins*` framework, cost modeling, and the `vsetvl`/AVL propagation passes together provide vector modes, intrinsics, autovectorization lowering, VL/VTYPE management, and vector-specific optimization. The module also includes processor tuning and scheduler descriptions for generic and named cores, frontend integration for C and D target macros/attributes, public intrinsic headers, extension-definition and documentation generators, and specialized RTL passes such as shorten-memrefs, save/restore cleanup, permutation-constant reuse, string operation expansion, and Zicfilp landing-pad insertion, making this directory the complete architecture-specific code-generation and target-semantics layer that distinguishes RISC-V from neighboring GCC target modules.
